d: To conduct inspections and monitor airside infrastructure, operations, and activities to ensure safe and efficient airside operations and compliance with GACAR Part 139 – Aerodromes, applicable ICAO standards, and airport safety procedures. The role supports aerodrome certification, operational safety oversight, continuous regulatory compliance, and the effective delivery of airside operations.
q: Bachelor’s degree or Diploma in Aviation Management, Aeronautical Engineering, Safety, or a related field.
Minimum 1-2 years’ experience in airside/aerodrome operations or aviation safety inspection
Knowledge of aerodrome inspection procedures and reporting standards.
Intermediate knowledge of Airside Safety and Operations.
Runway Surface Condition Assessment, Global reporting format (GRF).
Understanding of FOD prevention and wildlife hazard management.
Familiarity with airside vehicle control and operational safety procedures.
Proficiency in Microsoft Office and reporting tools.
r: Conduct daily and periodic airside inspections to verify the operational readiness of runways, taxiways, aprons, and associated safety areas.
Monitor runway surface conditions, lighting systems, signage, and pavement markings to ensure compliance with applicable aerodrome standards.
Identify and report Foreign Object Debris (FOD), wildlife hazards through regular wildlife monitoring patrols, and obstacle intrusions that may affect aircraft operations.
Verify that maintenance and construction activities within the airside area comply with approved safety procedures and applicable work permits.
Coordinate with relevant operational teams to initiate NOTAM requests when airfield conditions or ongoing works may affect aircraft operations.
Ensure that inspection findings and safety observations are properly documented, tracked, and reported in accordance with applicable aerodrome regulatory requirements.
Participate in the Aerodrome Safety Management System (SMS) by reporting hazards, conducting safety observations, and supporting safety risk assessments.
Escort unauthorized drivers within the airside area in accordance with related procedures.
Provide aircraft guidance using Follow-Me vehicles when required.
Monitor and report fuel spills and other hazardous substance spillages within the airside area.
Continuously monitor aircraft turnaround activities within the airside area and report any observed safety non-compliances.
Report airside incidents and occurrences and collect all available information to facilitate the investigation process.
Support emergency response activities in accordance with established airport emergency procedures.
Perform any other duties assigned by the Duty Supervisor and/or Direct Manager within the scope of the position.

d: The Executive Director, Client Coverage, Public Sector is the strategic adviser and relationship lead for a portfolio of major public sector clients, primarily across the Middle East and Pakistan. The portfolio includes central banks, ministries of finance, government entities and agencies, export credit and development agencies, multilateral organisations, regional development banks and selected development organisations. The role is accountable for developing senior client relationships, originating and delivering relevant solutions across Transaction Banking, Financial Markets and Global Banking, and achieving sustainable revenues and returns while maintaining strong credit, financial crime, conduct and regulatory risk discipline. The role also supports the regional team head on origination and client engagement across the region and selectively develops approved prospect relationships.
Lead client strategies through disciplined account planning and deliver agreed revenue, profitability, RoRWA and franchise objectives for the designated portfolio.

Build senior relationships up to ministerial and C-suite level, anticipate client needs, originate new business and position the Bank as a consistent strategic partner rather than a transactional provider.

Mobilise Transaction Banking, Financial Markets, Global Banking, structuring, advisory and industry partners to deliver relevant solutions, deepen inbound flows and selectively deploy balance sheet where supported by appropriate ancillary returns and Group economics.
Originate and structure sustainable finance solutions including debt-for-nature, debt-for-development and sustainable loans, and replicate successful structures across the public sector segment.

Own client acceptance and ongoing risk management, including AML, CDD and credit; maintain accurate account plans, call reports and deal pipelines; identify, escalate and resolve conduct, regulatory, reputational and credit issues.

Maintain strong knowledge of political, macroeconomic, country-risk and industry developments; bring international best practice, investment opportunities and thought leadership to clients; support investor roadshows, RFPs and industry engagement.

Maintain effective relationships with Country and Cluster leadership, Risk, Legal, Compliance, Client Management and product teams; ensure timely meeting notes, coordinated execution and high-quality client outcomes across the Bank network.

This is a senior individual-contributor role with no direct reports. The role holder is expected to contribute to team capability, knowledge sharing, diversity initiatives and the development of colleagues through informal coaching and collaboration.
Operate as a senior individual contributor, providing leadership through client judgement, execution discipline and collaboration across the regional Public Sector franchise.
Invest in personal development, share knowledge and support the development of colleagues through coaching, inclusive teamwork and participation in learning and diversity initiatives.
Maintain mandatory learning, professional development and risk-awareness standards applicable to the role.
Share sector, thematic and market insights with clients and internal partners to strengthen strategic engagement and the Bank’s market position.
Strategic client impact: Energised by solving complex public sector priorities and building trusted relationships with senior government, central bank and development-institution stakeholders.
Origination and innovation: Motivated by creating commercially sound, differentiated solutions across financing, markets, transaction banking and sustainable finance.
International collaboration: Thrives in a cross-border environment that requires judgement, resilience, teamwork and effective mobilisation of the Bank’s network.
q: 10+ years of relevant banking experience, preferably in senior relationship management, origination or sales covering public sector, sovereign, financial institution or development-finance clients.
Demonstrated experience managing complex client relationships, originating cross-product opportunities and coordinating execution across Transaction Banking, Financial Markets and Global Banking.
Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Banking, Finance, Economics, Business or a related discipline preferred.
Strong knowledge of credit, AML, CDD, conduct and regulatory requirements. Any market-specific licence required to undertake banking business must be maintained.
Arabic or other relevant regional language capability is advantageous.
